article_title: Predictors of the ethical use of generative artificial intelligence in higher education
citation: Tabares-Cruz YB, Cevallos-Sánchez HA, Arteaga-Pita IG, Rodriguez-Alava LA, Carreño-Mendoza AL, Cedeño-Barreto MdlÁ, Castro-Castillo GJ, Cobacango-Villavicencio JG and Moreira-Choez JS (2026) Predictors of the ethical use of generative artificial intelligence in higher education. Front. Educ. 11:1942426. https://doi.org/10.3389/feduc.2026.1942426
title: 44-item questionnaire measuring seven dimensions of ethical GenAI use
description: A newly developed self-administered instrument with 44 items across seven dimensions: six predictor constructs of six items each and an eight-item ethical-use dimension, answered on a five-point Likert scale. Reliability was satisfactory to high, with Cronbach's alpha ranging "from 0.861 for institutional guidance and ethics education to 0.924 for the ethical use of generative artificial intelligence," and composite reliability from 0.896 to 0.938. Seven reverse-worded items were retained after reverse-scoring.
requirements: Reverse-worded indicators must be reverse-scored before computing construct scores and reliability coefficients
constraints: The instrument was developed specifically for this study rather than adapted from a previously validated scale; validity evidence is from a single institutional sample
target_learners: university students at the State University of Milagro
target_learning_goals: measuring ethical, cognitive, self-regulatory, and institutional dimensions of generative AI use
examples: A sensitivity analysis showed excluding the reverse-worded indicator reduced Cronbach's alpha in every dimension, so no items were deleted

article_title: How Well Are Dental Students Equipped to Handle Traumatic Dental Injuries in Children?
citation: Zafar Sobia, Cheong Luan Lin Jovita, Ler Vonn, Teh Anastasia Min, Abbott Paul. (2026). How Well Are Dental Students Equipped to Handle Traumatic Dental Injuries in Children?. Australian Endodontic Journal. https://doi.org/10.1111/aej.70074
title: 44-item IADT-based TDI knowledge and confidence questionnaire
description: A 44-item questionnaire adapted from published studies based on the IADT guidelines, designed to comprehensively assess knowledge and confidence in TDI management across primary and permanent dentitions. It comprises five sections: demographics, primary dentition knowledge, fractures/subluxation knowledge, avulsion knowledge, and self-assessed confidence. The questionnaire was "piloted by administering it to 10 specialists endodontic (n = 5) and paediatric dentists (n = 5) who were asked to provide comments." Knowledge scores were categorised as Below average (0%–49.9%), Average (50%–74.9%) and Above average (75%–100%).
requirements: Pilot testing with specialist endodontists and paediatric dentists
constraints: Designed specifically for dental students who have completed a TDI module
target_learning_goals: Assessment of TDI management knowledge and confidence
key_sources: Zafar Sobia, Cheong Luan Lin Jovita, Ler Vonn, Teh Anastasia Min, Abbott Paul. (2026). How Well Are Dental Students Equipped to Handle Traumatic Dental Injuries in Children?. Australian Endodontic Journal. https://doi.org/10.1111/aej.70074
